problem: Two independent risk models described the same thing. build_management_risks (src/output/json/helpers.rs) produced summary.management_risks for the JSON, while compute_dimension_rows (src/output/pdf/single_report.rs) built the PDF's "Wichtigste Risiken" panel from a separate heuristic over severity counts and three module scores. They carried different dimensions, graded them differently, and the JSON's evidence-bearing rationales never reached the PDF reader. Two of the JSON dimensions also made claims the tool has no data for: "Trust / brand" was a fixed sentence citing no measurement, and "Project risk" inferred a component or template defect from repetition within a single page's DOM. Separately, derive_conversion_effect_from_action asserted conversion effects ("Klarere Navigation → weniger Absprünge", "Bessere Lesbarkeit → höhere Verweildauer") picked by substring-matching a localized recommendation string, for a tool with no analytics input at all.
evidence: reports/inros-lackner-audit.json generated 2026-09-19 (auditmysite v1.5.0): summary.management_risks held 4 high and 1 medium, while the PDF panel showed 3 bad and 2 warn over a partly different dimension set — "Trust / brand" and "Project risk" (both high) did not appear in the PDF at all, and two warn rows appeared that had no counterpart in the JSON. Every rationale string, with its numbers, was discarded. The PDF's module lookup used unwrap_or(100), so a module that never ran was rendered as a strength: test_management_summary_risks_and_strengths_split_for_mixed_report asserted exactly that, expecting "Sehr gute Auffindbarkeit" for a fixture with no SEO module. The conversion-effect claims reached no output format at all — 0 occurrences in both the JSON and the .typ — so they were unbacked claims computed as dead code.
expected: One derivation, in the analysis layer: audit::management_risk::build_management_risk_kinds returns ManagementRiskKind values carrying the raw numbers. Following #406, dimension(en) and rationale(en) are the single text source — the JSON calls them with en=true and keeps canonical English, the PDF re-derives in the run language from the same kind, so the German PDF never renders the stored English. Rationales name the values that set the tier. "Trust / brand" states that it is inferred from accessibility alone and that no brand signal is measured. "Project risk" only claims a component or template cause on multi-page runs, where recurrence across URLs is actually observed; on a single URL it reports findings with >=10 occurrences and says what would confirm a template cause. A dimension whose module did not run is RiskTier::Unknown and is excluded from both panels rather than counted as a risk or invented as a strength. The conversion-effect strings and derive_conversion_effect_from_action are deleted.
counter_examples: #576 must still hold: good dimensions belong in the strengths panel, never in the risks panel, and a report with no risks must render the zero-risk empty state rather than a padded-out fake risk.

A multi-page run must still be allowed to claim a component or template cause — that is the case where recurrence across URLs is real evidence; see project_risk_claims_a_template_cause_only_across_pages.
An English run must contain no German characters in either panel, and a German run must contain none of the canonical English rationale strings (#406).
